questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For my choice of destination, it was crucial that I could combine a good study environment with a high level of academic quality.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I remember it as quite easy. But I believe that it is always a bit difficult finding information at University websites other than the one you are used to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators were ready to welcome us at the University on the first day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The University offered an off-campus housing. I got the housing through their housing lottery.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think I can recommend anything here. My housing was an off-campus housing but in collaboration with the University. Therefore, I was in a building with a lot of other students, which I really do recommend as there is a lot of community through the building. Also it feels quite safe that you are surrounded by other follow students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was quite easy. The university sent us emails every time we needed to take action or register somewhere, which made the whole process easier. The entire course registration portal was also easy to use, and we were guided through it. However, it was a bit difficult to understand the university’s block system. It was divided into three blocks, but there were only courses available for exchange students in two of them. This caused confusion during the registration process and was also not ideal in terms of course planning in the block where we had to overload in order to reach our required ECTS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators were very helpfull to answer questions through mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration process was very easy. I had one course i wanted but didn't get due to limited seats.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the time to familiarize yourself with it, and if possible, discuss it with other exchange students from your home university. It can be a bit confusing to navigate on your own when it’s not something you’re used to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were quite a bit more difficult than expected, and there wasn’t really any consideration given to whether you were an exchange student or not. This put a lot of pressure on the exams, as it took quite a lot just to pass. It was a bit of an unfortunate ending that the majority of the exchange group had to resit at least one exam. If you choose UvA, you should definitely be prepared for some challenging courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They were pretty similar. Seminars and lectures. Some course were only lectures, but otherwise it was quite the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Private International Law definitely. It was a pretty rough course but definitely the course I got the most out of.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open minded, don't go to easy on the courses, explore the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
